correctness.rationale: Detailed balance gives π_{k+1}/π_k=(n−k)(a+bk)/(k+1). The sign above one is a concave quadratic in k (decreasing affine at b=0), with initial sign na−1 and limiting sign negative at k=n. If na≥1 there is one modal component. If na<1 the first edge is strictly downhill, and a separated positive-count component exists exactly when at least one k≥1 edge strictly rises, i.e. b>min h(k). The positive edges form one block; exact ties can widen a plateau but cannot create a second rising block. In particular equality at b_c gives a nonincreasing law and n=2 allows a second mode at the upper endpoint. With c=1−na, the derivative of h has sign (1+a)k²+2ck−nc, which gives z_* and the clipped two-candidate rule. At a=λ/n with fixed 0<λ<1, z_*=√(cn)−c+O(n⁻¹ᐟ²), h(z_*)=c/z_*² and integer rounding costs O(n⁻⁵ᐟ²) by the second derivative near z_*; this gives the stated expansion. The minimizing k is an edge index, not necessarily the exact position of a mode. The mean-field drift has opposite signs at 0 and n and is concave (strictly decreasing affine when b=0), so it has one feasible zero. The conventional 1/(n−1) comparison is not a bifurcation in that imported ODE. Frozen checker and recorded results were read but not executed; the candidate test there uses a float square root. `python3 /workspace/branches/review_reproduction.py 2` separately verified exact derivative signs, ties at every adjacent-mass equality in its finite grid, and strict and plateau modal witnesses.
